title: NVIDIA Reveals How DLSS 5 Neural Rendering Works at SIGGRAPH 2026
excerpt: The AI-powered upgrade uses a diffusion transformer model to add photorealistic lighting to games in real time and ships this fall with support from Bethesda, Capcom, and Ubisoft.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • NVIDIA's DLSS 5 uses a diffusion transformer model for real-time neural rendering.
  • The technology enhances game visuals with photorealistic lighting at up to 4K resolution.
  • Developers have granular controls to maintain artistic intent in their games.
  • Major publishers like Bethesda and Capcom are integrating DLSS 5 into upcoming titles.

NVIDIA SIGGRAPH 2026 Keynote
  • NVIDIA demonstrated DLSS 5 technical details at its SIGGRAPH 2026 keynote, revealing a distilled one-step diffusion transformer model for real-time neural rendering.
  • The technology adds photorealistic lighting and materials to game frames in real time at up to 4K resolution and ships this fall.
  • Developers get granular controls including intensity sliders, color grading, and per-object masking to preserve artistic intent.
  • Bethesda, Capcom, Ubisoft, and other major publishers have committed to integrating DLSS 5 in upcoming titles.

From Upscaling to Neural Rendering

NVIDIA used its 2026 SIGGRAPH Research Keynote to pull back the curtain on DLSS 5, detailing for the first time how the company's most ambitious graphics technology actually works. First unveiled at GTC in March, the technology moved from marketing pitch to full technical demonstration at SIGGRAPH, with the engineers who built it explaining its architecture on stage.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=8oNgaiTx3js

Edward Liu, NVIDIA's Director of Applied Deep Learning Research and the architect behind the DLSS line, explained that version 5 represents a fundamental shift. Previous iterations focused on AI-driven upscaling, ray reconstruction, and frame generation — technologies that boost performance. DLSS 5 adds a new category entirely: using a generative AI model to enhance the visual quality of rendered frames in real time.

"The renderer keeps building the world exactly as the game has authored it. The generation becomes the learned stage afterwards to enrich its appearance."

— Edward Liu, Director of Applied Deep Learning Research, NVIDIA

"Liu described it as a distilled one-step pixel-space diffusion transformer model, optimized specifically for photorealism within the tight performance budgets of real-time rendering."

How It Works

The model takes a game's color output and motion vectors as input, then applies learned enhancements to lighting, materials, and surface properties. Liu said the system draws on internal renderer buffers — albedo, surface normals, and lighting information — to preserve scene details while improving elements such as subsurface scattering on skin, fabric sheen, contact shadows, and light-material interactions on hair.

https://www.instagram.com/p/Da6KnAQE4De/

DLSS 5 runs causally, processing one frame at a time without looking ahead, a hard requirement for interactive gaming. Liu described it as a distilled one-step pixel-space diffusion transformer model, optimized specifically for photorealism within the tight performance budgets of real-time rendering. The company had to solve three core challenges: preserving the developer's artistic intent, maintaining temporal coherence from frame to frame, and fitting within the roughly 16-millisecond window of a 60-fps game.

"DLSS 5 is the GPT moment for graphics — blending hand-crafted rendering with generative AI to deliver a dramatic leap in visual realism while preserving the control artists need for creative expression," CEO Jensen Huang said in his opening remarks.

Developer Controls Take Center Stage

Developer Control Features
›Intensity sliders for structure and tone.
›Selective effects using masks on characters.
›Different models for various scenes.
›Integration with existing Streamline framework.

A significant portion of the SIGGRAPH presentation addressed an early concern about AI rendering: that it would override artists' creative decisions. NVIDIA demonstrated that developers can adjust structure intensity and tone intensity through two main sliders, select different models for different scenes or cutscenes, and apply effects selectively using masks on specific characters, props, or sections of an environment.

"DLSS 5 is fully controllable from the developer," said Gaff, a creative artist who demonstrated the tools at the keynote. Integration uses NVIDIA's existing Streamline framework, the same pipeline already deployed for current DLSS and Reflex implementations.

Game Support and NVIDIA's Broader AI Push

Major publishers including Bethesda, Capcom, Tencent, Ubisoft, and Warner Bros. Games have committed to DLSS 5. Confirmed titles include Starfield, Resident Evil Requiem, Hogwarts Legacy, Assassin's Creed Shadows, Phantom Blade Zero, and The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion Remastered, among over a dozen others.

"When NVIDIA showed us DLSS 5 and we got it running in Starfield, it was amazing how it brought it to life," said Todd Howard, studio head at Bethesda Game Studios. Capcom executive Jun Takeuchi called it "another important step in pushing visual fidelity forward."

Beyond gaming, NVIDIA used the SIGGRAPH keynote to expand its Cosmos world foundation model platform. The company announced Cosmos 3 Edge, a four-billion-parameter model built to run in real time on devices such as Jetson Thor for robotics and video analytics without requiring a data center round trip. It also demonstrated AI physics simulations capable of predicting engineering outcomes more than 10,000 times faster than traditional methods.

DLSS 5 arrives this fall, bringing what NVIDIA frames as a step toward closing the visual gap between real-time games and Hollywood visual effects — a gap that raw hardware horsepower alone has never bridged.
